cards.text: Last time, Joseph's brothers came back to Egypt with Benjamin, their youngest brother, and feasted with Joseph. They STILL have no idea the man in charge is Joseph, the brother they sold (Gen 37:28; 42:8; 43:34). Now Joseph, ruler over the land (Gen 42:6), tells his steward to fill the men's sacks with as much food as they can carry.

cards.question: Joseph also tells the steward to put each man's ___ back in the mouth of his sack.

cards.text: Then Joseph adds one more thing, just for the youngest one's sack. That's Benjamin, Joseph's own mother's son (Gen 43:29).

cards.question: What does Joseph have the steward slip into Benjamin's sack?

cards.text: At daybreak the brothers head home with their donkeys, and they're not far from the city when Joseph sends his steward chasing after them. It's like walking out of a store and the alarm goes BEEP, and you have NO idea why.

cards.question: Joseph gives the steward a question to throw at the brothers when he catches them. What is it?

answers.text: Why have you repaid good with evil
Why did you leave before the dawn
Why did you lie about your brother

cards.text: He's also told to say this is the cup his master drinks from and uses for divination, and then, "What you have done is wicked!" The steward catches up and says it all, just like Joseph told him.

cards.question: True or false: When the steward accuses them, the brothers admit they took the cup and ask for mercy.
To prove they're honest men, what do the brothers remind the steward of?

answers.text: They brought back the silver they found
They never once left the steward's sight
They swore an oath before Pharaoh himself

cards.text: Then the brothers go ALL in: if any of them is found with it, he dies, and the rest become slaves. Friend, never bet your life on a bag somebody else packed.

cards.question: True or false: The steward agrees that if the cup turns up, the rest of the brothers will become slaves too.

cards.text: Every brother drops his sack to the ground and opens it FAST. The steward starts with the oldest and works his way down… one sack… the next… the next…

cards.question: The steward finds the cup in ___ sack.
True or false: Once the cup turns up, the brothers leave Benjamin with the steward and keep heading home.

cards.text: Nope. They tear their clothes, load up the donkeys, and the WHOLE crew turns around and walks back to the city, and not one of them says, "Well, it was nice knowing you, Benjamin."
Judah, one of the brothers, and the rest of them fall to the ground before Joseph, who's still at his house. Joseph asks, "What is this deed you have done?"

cards.question: Judah doesn't argue or make excuses to Joseph. What does Judah say God has done?

answers.text: Exposed the iniquity of his servants
Hidden the cup inside Benjamin's sack
Sent this great man to test them all

cards.question: Judah tells Joseph they are now his slaves. Who does Judah include?

answers.text: All the brothers along with Benjamin
Only the oldest of the brothers

cards.text: Joseph answers, "Far be it from me to do this." Then he lays out his own terms.

cards.question: Joseph rules that the man found with the cup will be his slave, and the rest of the brothers may return to their father in ___.

cards.text: Then Judah steps right up to Joseph and says, "Do not be angry with your servant, for you are equal to Pharaoh himself." Friend, THAT is how you open when you're about to ask the boss for something HUGE.
Judah starts at the beginning: Joseph once asked if they had a father or a brother. They told him about an elderly father and a younger brother, the child of his old age.

cards.question: The brothers also told Joseph that the boy's brother is ___.

cards.text: Let that sink in. They're telling JOSEPH that Joseph is dead, and he has to stand there and just… nod.

cards.question: True or false: When Joseph told them to bring the boy down, the brothers warned that if the boy left his father, his father would die.

cards.text: But Joseph said unless the younger brother came down, they would not see his face again. So when food ran low back home, their father said, "Go back and buy us some food."

cards.question: True or false: The brothers told their father they could go see the man without their younger brother.

cards.text: Then Judah repeats what their father, Jacob, told them (Gen 42:29). It starts, "You know that my wife bore me two sons."

cards.question: Jacob says one of his two sons was gone. What did Jacob say had happened to him?

answers.text: He'd been lost in the desert

cards.question: Jacob says if they take Benjamin too and harm comes to him, what will that do to Jacob?

answers.text: Send him to his grave in sorrow
Make him leave Canaan for good
Turn him against all of his sons

cards.text: Judah lays it out: their father's life is wrapped up in the boy's life. If Jacob sees the boy isn't with them, he will die.

cards.question: Then Judah tells Joseph something Judah did back home with his father. What was it?

answers.text: He paid the man's silver himself
He promised to bring double food

cards.text: If he didn't bring the boy home, Judah said he'd bear the guilt before his father all his life. Friend, Judah didn't just make a promise. He CO-SIGNED for his little brother.

cards.question: So here it comes, Judah's big ask. What does Judah beg Joseph to do?

answers.text: Keep Judah as a slave in place of the boy
Let the brothers buy the boy back later
Take their donkeys in place of the boy

cards.question: True or false: Judah asks Joseph to let the boy go back home with his brothers.

cards.text: Years ago, Judah was the one who said to sell Joseph (Gen 37:26-27). Now he's begging to be the slave so his father's youngest son can go home.

cards.question: Judah asks how he can go back to his father without the boy. He says he could not bear to see the ___ that would overwhelm his father.

cards.text: And that's where Judah stops, with Joseph's answer still hanging in the air. Stick with me, friend, because this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'If he didn't bring the boy home… all his life.' / 'Friend, Judah didn't just make a promise.' / 'He CO-SIGNED for his little brother.' Only the opening card may run to 3 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This card tells nothing new from the passage. It only reacts to Genesis 44:20, which card 3 already covered. The joke has no passage moment of its own to ride on.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The second sentence restates Genesis 44:33, which cards 14 and 15 already asked about. The only new content is the Genesis 37:26-27 connection, so the card works as a recap and doesn't move the passage forward. The connection could ride along on a card that tells passage content.

The right answer, 'Exposed the iniquity of his servants', sounds much more like the Bible than the plain wrong answers ('Hidden the cup inside Benjamin's sack', 'Sent this great man to test them all'), so it stands out. Also, 'his servants' is unclear. In the text, Judah says 'your servants', meaning the brothers as Joseph's servants. With 'his', the baker can't tell whose servants are meant (God's, Judah's or Joseph's).

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
